subtopics.title: Closed, Open, and the Four Participants

questions.question: An OPEN economy differs from a closed economy because it includes:
options: The foreign sector — exports and imports

questions.question: The four markets in which the participants meet are:
options: The factor market, the product market, the financial market and the foreign exchange market

questions.question: The REAL flow in the circular flow diagram consists of:
options: Factor services moving one way and goods and services moving the other — things, not money

questions.question: Households' role in the four-sector model is to:
options: Produce goods and buy capital equipment
Collect taxes and provide public goods
Own and supply the factors of production, earn wages, rent, interest and profit, then consume, save and pay tax

subtopics.title: Leakages, Injections and the Equilibrium Condition

questions.question: The three leakages from the circular flow are:
The equilibrium condition for the four-sector economy is:
options: S + T + M = I + G + X
T = G and M = X separately

questions.question: Saving of R300bn, taxation R500bn, imports R400bn; investment R350bn, government spending R550bn, exports R300bn. The economy is:
options: In equilibrium — leakages of R1 200bn equal injections of R1 200bn
Impossible to judge without the consumption figure

questions.question: The trap examiners set with the pairs (S–I, T–G, M–X) is that:
options: Only the TOTAL of the three leakages must equal the TOTAL of the three injections — individual pairs need not match

subtopics.title: Measuring the Flow — Three Methods, Three Aggregates

questions.question: The production method must sum value ADDED rather than total sales because:
options: Otherwise intermediate goods are counted twice

questions.question: GDP at market prices is R6 000bn, taxes on products R700bn and subsidies on products R100bn. GDP at factor cost is:
With GDP at market prices of R6 000bn, primary income received from abroad of R80bn and primary income paid abroad of R200bn, GNI equals:
Nominal GDP is R6 000bn and the deflator is 120 (base 100). Real GDP is:
options: R5 000bn — and if real GDP grows more slowly than population, output per person falls

questions.question: When leakages exceed injections, the sequence runs:
options: Unsold stock → production cut → retrenchment → falling incomes → smaller leakages → equilibrium at a LOWER national income
Rising prices → higher wages → higher output
Higher exports → stronger rand → more imports

questions.question: Whether an increase in injections raises OUTPUT or mainly raises PRICES depends on:
options: The size of the government sector
Whether the economy has idle capacity or is already near full capacity

questions.question: "The flow is self-correcting in direction but not in outcome" means:
options: The economy always finds a new equilibrium, but it may settle at high unemployment — balance is not the same as a good result
Prices always return to their original level

questions.question: Fiscal policy, monetary policy and trade policy are alike in that each:
options: Is controlled by the Reserve Bank
Works only in a closed economy
Moves a leakage or an injection — G and T, S and I through interest rates, and X and M respectively

subtopics.title: The Money That Goes Around the Township

questions.question: The "two rings turning in opposite directions" are:
options: One carrying work and goods, the other carrying rands

questions.question: A Friday wage spent at the spaza shows that:
options: Money is used up when spent
Money circulates — it returns to a business and becomes somebody else's wage
The spaza is part of the foreign sector

questions.question: In the Friday-wage picture, the foreign sector appears as:
options: Imported fuel in the taxi and coal leaving by ship

questions.question: In the bath analogy, the LEVEL of the water represents:
options: National income — the size of the economy

questions.question: The three taps are:
options: Business investment, government spending and export earnings

questions.question: The bath "sits still" when:
options: Each tap matches its own drain exactly
The taps TOGETHER match the drains TOGETHER — saving may exceed investment provided the other flows make up the difference

questions.question: Measuring the water three ways — made, earned, spent — corresponds to:
options: Nominal, real and per capita GDP
The production, income and expenditure methods, which should agree

subtopics.title: When the Bucket Won't Sit Still

questions.question: Exports falling from R300bn to R250bn starts the chain:
options: Goods unsold → shift cut → smaller wages → less spent at the spaza → smaller orders, round after round

questions.question: The bath settles again at a lower level because:
options: Falling incomes automatically mean less saved, less tax paid and fewer imports — the drains narrow to match the taps

questions.question: If factories are already running flat out, extra spending mainly produces:
options: Higher PRICES — the extra money cannot buy extra goods

questions.question: A weaker rand that makes our exports cheaper abroad is, in tap-and-drain language:
options: A wider EXPORT tap — an injection into the flow
